messages:
anna: FYI, after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak we're seeing intermittent OOMs on our long-chat perf suite :frowning:
anna: Root cause looks like interaction between PyTorch/CUDA allocator knobs and the new workspace sizing heuristics. repro attached.
raj: ack, can you paste the failing log + the exact knob values used in the run?
anna: here — run command and key envs:```env RUN_SUITE=long-chat ./bench/run_perf.sh --model redwood-7b``````export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=\"max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_threshold:0.7\"
expandable_segments = true (set inside runtime config)
```
marta: thanks. quick note: garbage_collection_threshold is a fraction we apply in our allocator wrapper, 0.7 means GC triggers less often. that can leave more fragmented free blocks.
sam: repro log (trimmed):```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.42 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 12.10 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 1536.00 MiB reserved in non-releasable caches)
Traceback (most recent call last): ...```
sam: also saw a repeated pattern: small allocations spike during KV cache warmup, then a big kernel for decoding fails — looks like sawtooth but not exactly the old one.
raj: interesting. did we change continuous-batching thresholds? kernel selector can increase temporary workspace for certain attention kernels.
anna: yes, selector now prefers fwd-optim kernels above seq_len 1024 which request bigger temp buffers.
marta: hypothesis: with expandable_segments=true + high max_split_size_mb we end up with fewer but larger splits, which fragments when many small allocations happen (KV warmup) and then the large kernel can't find contiguous region.
ci-bot: perf-run 1864527001 completed — artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1864527001/logs.tar.gz
raj: can we repro locally with smaller mem? try forcing max_split_size_mb=16 and GC threshold=0.3 to see if fragmentation reduces.
anna: trying now. switching to: `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=\"max_split_size_mb:16,garbage_collection_threshold:0.3\"` and runtime flag `--expandable-segments=false`
sam: quick profiling snapshot (from nvprof / CUPTI-like):```Kernel: attention_opt   temp_alloc_peak=1.1GB   alloc_count=124   avg_alloc=9.1MB
KV_warmup small allocs: alloc_count=860   avg_alloc=24KB
free_count spikes right before decoding kernel
```
marta: that matches fragmentation. small allocations fill holes between splits because of allocation strategy, frees leave many small free ranges. when attention_opt asks for a 1.1GB contiguous temp buffer it fails.
raj: possible mitigations: 1) aggressive GC before big kernels (manual torch.cuda.empty_cache()/our GC wrapper), 2) reduce max_split_size_mb so splits are smaller/denser, 3) enable compaction step that merges adjacent free blocks (expensive), 4) prefer kernel variants with lower temp buffer needs.
anna: quick test results: with max_split_size_mb=16 + GC 0.3 + expandable_segments=false the run completed 6/6 times locally (was failing 3/6 before). latency slightly worse (~4% tail).
sam: tradeoff acceptable for now. but we need automated detection: runtime should detect imminent big-kernel allocation and pre-run a GC/compaction if fragmentation > threshold.
marta: agreed. implementation sketch: track free-run-length histogram; on allocation request > X% of GPU mem or > Y MB, run GC and if still failing fall back to lower-temp kernel or chunked-kernel path.
raj: also add a perf-test variant to CI that toggles a few knob combos to catch regressions — e.g., (expandable_segments true/false) x (max_split_size_mb 16/64/128) x (garbage_collection_threshold 0.3/0.7).
anna: I'll open a RFC with the detection + fallback plan. also adding bench cases to stress KV warmup pattern.
sam: can we add a small runtime metric for "frag_score" (0..1) computed from free ranges so we can trigger GC conservatively?
marta: yes — can be a moving window. we already expose largest_free_block and total_free. frag_score = 1 - (largest_free / total_free).
raj: nice. add telemetry tagging so we can correlate frag_score spikes with recent deploys.

anna: thanks — I'll run the targeted perf-suite on staging with the conservative config and report back. :eyes:
sam: thx all. next steps: anna opens RFC + PR for pre-kernel GC; raj adds CI matrix perf runs; marta prototypes frag_score metric.
anna: filing threads: RFC-卷-237 (will paste link), perf run id when done.
